output.brief:
The October night premium shortfalls were caused by a pay rule change, not by Fenmarch's data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule NSP-02. The template moved the start of the premium window from 20:00 to 22:00. The change was logged as a "label correction" with no calculation impact and no testing. The platform audit trail records it as the only pay-rule edit in the period. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 staff who start at 22:00 were paid correctly. Re-running October with the window set back to 20:00 matched expected pay for all 158. Flagged data records show no link to the errors. Release 7.4 and the bank file are not implicated.

Do not suspend the HR team, re-cleanse the data, or accept the clause 14.3 cost. Do not roll back release 7.4, because the November tax table update needs it. Instead, have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start, verify it in the test tenant, and make off-cycle back-payments to the 147. Also review how Ardentra's change entries are approved. Whether the rota trial or the premium shortfall is driving the fall in night overtime cover is still unclear. I would not pause the trial yet. I'm confident in this diagnosis.
